name: Healthcare practice
description: A doctor's, dental or physiotherapy practice: the team, the services, a price list and patients' questions, with facts about insurers, new patients and appointments.

questions.question: Which health insurers do you have contracts with?
questions.help: List them as patients know them, separated by commas. Write "none – self-paying patients only" if you have no contracts.

questions.question: Are you accepting new patients at the moment?
questions.help: For example "yes", "no" or "only children under 15". Patients look for this first – keep it up to date.

questions.question: Do you have an online booking system? Give its address.
questions.help: Leave it empty if patients book by phone.

questions.question: Which number should patients call outside surgery hours?
questions.help: The out-of-hours service or emergency line you refer patients to.

questions.question: What are the specialisations of your practice?
In which languages can patients talk to you?
Since which year has the practice been open?

audit.message: Say which health insurers you have contracts with – patients check this before anything else.
Say whether you are accepting new patients.
Add your surgery hours in Business details.
Add the doctors and staff to the team – patients want to know who will treat them.
The price list has not changed for a year – check the prices of services not covered by insurance.
A practice handles health data – publish a privacy policy page (how patient data is processed) and check what your regulations require.

claude: Patients come to a practice site to find out whether their insurer is accepted, whether new patients are taken, the surgery hours and how to book – put these first and keep them as facts so they are stated the same everywhere. Write calmly and plainly; never give medical advice, diagnose, recommend treatments or promise outcomes, and describe services as what the practice offers, not what it guarantees. Do not invent doctors, qualifications, specialisations, insurers, prices or patient reviews – ask the owner for every such detail. Health data is sensitive: forms should ask only for what an appointment needs and the privacy page must say how patient data is handled. When something may be required by health or data-protection regulations, say that it should be checked rather than stating it as law.
